comment: Regression: -A (previously selected fingerprints) was read but never
applied, so output was byte identical to omitting -A, and the first
record reported the DIST<1> placeholder instead of a real distance.
data/prior.gfp and data/pool.gfp are disjoint halves of
data/pubchem_example.gfp, so no pair is at distance zero and every
seeded distance is meaningful. -h 1 because selection order among
equidistant candidates is not reproducible with multiple threads.
test.name: previously_selected

comment: Regression: a -A file yielding no fingerprints used to be reported as
success, silently leaving every initial distance at 1.0 - which is
indistinguishable from -A never having been given. It must fail now.
Driven by a shell script so the exit status and the diagnostic can be
asserted without embedding absolute paths in the golden output.
Covers an empty file and a file that is not TDT at all.
test.name: previously_selected_no_fingerprints

comment: Regression: with -p (distance scaling factors) the tool selects via
spread_with_weights, which fills selected_item[] rather than writing
as it goes. An unconditional early return sat in front of the code
that wrote that array, so -p produced no output whatsoever.
Weights are all 1.0, so this must reproduce the unweighted ordering.
test.name: weights_uniform

comment: -p together with -A. Exercises two further faults in that path: the
first selection has no in-pool neighbour so nearest_previously_selected
stays -1, which used to be used to index fingerprints[-1]; and the -A
seed distances arrived unweighted while every later update was weighted.
Weights are all 1.0 here, so the distances must match those of
previously_selected.
test.name: weights_previously_selected

comment: Non-uniform weights must steer the first selection under -A: the pick
is argmax(weight * seed distance). PBCHM129016465 has weight 1.0 and
every other pool member 0.001, so it has to be selected first. Before
the fix the first-point scan compared a weighted value against an
unweighted running maximum, and seeded its index at 1 rather than 0.
test.name: weights_skewed_previously_selected

comment: Regression: -b was parsed after the spread had already run and written
its output, so brief output was silently ignored and full TDT was
emitted instead of 'smiles id dist'.
test.name: brief
weights_skewed_brief
comment: Weighted brief output uses the same four-decimal distance formatting as TDT output.

test.name: weights_above_one
comment: Weights and weighted distances above one use stable fallback formatting.
